newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil soy crop may rise as much as 12 pct - Cardoso.
newsitem.headline: Brazil soy crop may rise as much as 12 pct - Cardoso.

text.p: Brazil's soybean harvest in 1996/97 should show an increase of 10 to 12 percent from last year's levels, said President Fernando Henrique Cardoso in his weekly radio program.
Cardoso did not give an exact figure for the crop but said Agriculture Minister Arlindo Porto would announce the government's forecast for the 1996/97 grains and oilseeds harvest on Wednesday.
Given last year's soybean crop was put at around 23 million tonnes, a 10 to 12 percent increase would suggest a 1996/97 harvest of up to 25.76 million tonnes.
This would compare with an estimate of 26 million tonnes from the U.S. Department of Agriculture and 26.38 million tonnes by independent Brazilian consultants Safras e Mercado.

One of the reasons for the rise is the scrapping of a state export tax in September to stimulate exports, Cardoso said. "Prices internationally are high and without the state tax, the farmer has become enthusiastic about planting."
Cardoso also spoke of a higher wheat harvest of 3.17 million tonnes.
-- Caroline Bulloch, Rio de Janeiro newsroom, 5521 5074151
